title: fix: stop pending database writes when shutdown starts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a pending agent database write committing after root-wide asynchronous close begins while a retained resource is still draining.

## User Impact

Database shutdown rejects pending native writes as soon as close begins and still waits for retained resources to finish. Schemas, persisted formats, and update behavior are unchanged; no migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root-wide close previously awaited resource drainage before revoking pending native opens. Revoke matching opens synchronously, as exact-path close already does, while preserving the existing drain and native-join loop, cleanup ownership, and selected-root isolation.

## Evidence

The two gated real-SQLite regressions failed on the original code: both selected-root and global close allowed the write to resolve `written` instead of rejecting. Both pass with the fix, including native settlement, lease release, blocked close completion, and absence of persisted writes.

All 56 tests across open authority, resource lifecycle, and admission ordering pass. Independent P2 review is clean. The full selected changed-file gate passed, including production and test typechecks, scoped lint, unused-export scans, and storage/import guards. A normal frozen dependency install resolved the initial borrowed-install declaration-boundary refusal.

The [initial CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35424341289/job/105847686138) failed `github-repository-publication.test.ts` with a session publication-exclusion timeout (575 ms test duration). Its exact merge was `0b5f6f3c5a29` (this head onto parent `debd174b3af4`). The unchanged 44-case file passed locally on both that merge and parent. An isolated Linux replay of the recovered 98-file group passed all 1,351 tests on the merge with acquisition diagnostics and a process-local `0022` umask. Separate cleanup failures under the Testbox's inherited `0002` umask reproduced on both merge and parent and were traced to group-writable fixture directories; the unchanged five-case file passed under `0022`.

The [single diagnostic failed-job rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35424341289/job/105870514288), attempt 2, passed without source, timeout, assertion, or gate changes. The original exclusion failure's cause remains unresolved; these passes do not establish that it was unrelated. Both the isolated probe and the rerun used 4 CPUs/about 16 GB, whereas the initial failure used 8 CPUs/about 32 GB, so the original hardware condition was not reproduced.
